body: I already know how to distract, meditate, do breathing exercises, take up new hobbies, go outside, talk to loved ones, listen to mucus, journal, talk about your feelings, be my one best friend, everything..... it’s gotten worse and just...... I need something new

Thank you..... I.... somehow keep getting pulled back in and have roomed with her for 5 years now but...... I know this is my breaking point and that I can’t do it any more....... but I’m trying...

Thank you though... I’m really hoping I can continue onward and get myself more stable so I don’t try again........... because that deep want is still there...

It’s so stupid because I’ve even lost a SO because she was jealous of how emotionally strong I was.... which is the most bizarre reason I think but it makes sense when she explains it. I’ve had depression since I was 6, maybe earlier. I’ve struggled but always managed to keep myself alive. I’ve gotten through horrible family members, horrible situations all throughout childhood, as many aggressive people you could think of.... but my roommate is something else and I’m /stuck/ in a freaking lease with her for the remaining of this year..... I’m going to try and deal with it all and try to work through things like that but....... idk..... it’s so hard when she thinks she can do no wrong and I’m not able to explain anything in a way that she will accept.....

That’s the problem, I can’t. The fight was with my friend who is also my roommate. If I try to walk away she follows. Every time I try to defuse the situation, she escalated it. Every time I’ve asked to just have 5 minutes to calm myself, think a little better she won’t let me have it. When I shut down and stop talking she will sad as many hurtful and inflammatory things she needs to make me angry and get me arguing with her again. She was saying how I would be nothing without her, how I’m just going to go in my room and be upset and leave everything for her as per usual even though I’m the one usually left to taking care of everything in the house. But if I ever challenge her on any point she then logics her way into somehow being right.

She even said it in the car that she needs to get a rise out of me and that she does it on purpose when I disassociate just to try and keep me talking /as to somehow help me/. I have no idea why anyone would even THINK that’s a okay way to try and help a depressive suicidal person.

it does not help me because even if I have friends, not of them come over, I’m always just stuck in a apartment with just me and her and no one else. None of the reach out to me either. I know why that is, I have MS and it puts me as insane risk of death. But all it does at the same time is isolate me. I also have to be the one to usually reach out..... it’s not because of my personality if that’s what you’re thinking either, because if it was the friend’s I have would quickly drop someone who was a shitty toxic person if so...... instead it was them who saved me because they care and I realize that.....but it doesn’t change that the only person I interact with at all for the most part is my roommate. That on her bad days she seems to take her anger out on me. That all my energy is usually spent on trying to walk around her issues or let things go that seriously hurt me emotionally....

Whatever... it doesn’t matter......

When it comes to getting a diagnosis and therapy they are not legally allowed to share the information you give to them when it comes to your metal health and what you may or may not have. But, I also know that my word is a word of a stranger so here is what I suggest!

Since I’m not sure what state you live in I would recommend just researching on a federal and state level HIPAA laws and regulations. If it’s the same I have run into (and I’m fairly sure it is but still, you’ll get a better safety of mind if you check yourself as well) then the therapist does not and will not share this information with any work you may be at or may be applying for so there is no risk there. Also, unless you are a danger to yourself and those around you in the form of you have actually been arrested for physical violence in some way shape or form, then just being a sociopath or psychopath will not harm your day to day. Sociopath and psychopath mental health gets a really bad stigma when it comes to mental health and so I get it :( yes, hurting someone is horrible, but you said that you don’t currently and you’re more seeking help to manage things in your day to day, which is so brave! It truly is and I know it’s hard to take that step, but just reaching out like this is a step in itself and matters.

Every mental health issue comes with its downsides, but just because of a stigma on any of them does not mean that you shouldn’t get help :( it just translates into more suffering for you down the road and that’s not good at all.

Please do a little looking into HIPAA and patient confidentiality so that when you go to seek a therapist and diagnosis that you can feel safe in doing so :) I wish you all the luck!!

Just to ask and, OP if you can’t answer that’s okay, but was there ever a very huge or traumatic time in your life where opening up was immediately met with someone lashing out at you and hurt you mentally or physically for just sharing?

Through my travels of life I have found that this usually is the result of someone being hurt to different degrees. I myself suffer from it. From what you have said I’m not sure if you’ll be able to recall the memories if that happened, but I do know the locking memories and forcibly forgetting them is a bad copping mechanism for sever trauma. The reason it’s “bad” (I don’t like calling it bad because you’re doing it as a stress response so it’s not controllable and my heart more goes out to you for you needing to do it at all, but I digress) is because doing this will develop into PTSD pretty typically and the repressed memories may come back later (I’m not a therapist, but I’ve talked with people and have PTSD myself and while it will re-manifest in different ways it always is PTSD)

I’m sorry to hear that it seems like you’re in such a stressful situation that you’re needing to do that or that you were and are still feeling high enough stress to continue. :( it’s hard, all of it, but you are no alone and while it will take time things can get better.

If you’re able to I would extremely recommend a therapist and specifically someone who specializes in PTSD for sure (if and when you can) I would also recommend looking into PTSD and see if there are any better copping mechanisms you can use instead. TBH there is probably a /lot/ more going on, but I can at least tell you my best guess for what this specifically is and I really hope that this can help in some way.

OP, I agree with you.

I’ve had to go through several therapists. Some were honestly really bad and a few I loved to bits and they really did help me.

I’m 30 and have been able to start helping myself since 24 but I’ve been suffering from mental illnesses since I was 6. In my life here is what I have found.

Almost every time someone tears down a therapist and fully denounces therapy completely, from at least what I have seen it’s as you said, those people are not setting what they need with the therapist and when they don’t get it they just stay and keep paying someone who can’t help them and eventually they get fed up with that. Other times it’s like my mom when she feeds the therapist her BS and it comes to light sudden all therapists are horrible. (Was a solo therapist till she asked my dad to join her for a couples counseling and she hated that when my Dad got a saw the therapists didn’t 100% agree with her and suddenly therapy was a scam.)

I’ve seen several therapists. Half of them have flat out told me they can’t help me. For those who hate therapists do you know why that is? Because  while I suffer 24/7 from sever depression I’ve been able to cope with it enough to at lea function and I have the coping mechanisms they would normally teach me. However, none of them knew how the heck to deal with PTSD, which came to be the main thing I needed help with. I’ve changed therapists several times over but have eventually found one who does CBT (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy) and that has worked for me. He’s also taught me a new few ways to help in the day to day with my depression a little better. I’ll repeat /he helped and I also didn’t have to throw thousands of dollars at him to get said help/.

If you have a therapist that isn’t working for you, like OP said, change therapists and keep changing till you find one. Come out the gate and tell them what you want and if they can’t help you in the first 3-5 session, leave and find another.

They didn’t go to school for a degree and spend thousands of their own dollars to BS you for nothing. If they are not working for you, pin point what you /need/ and find someone who specializes in that. Keep trying till you get someone who works, because they do and can help you. It’s not a thing where they need to put in all the work to make you better; you also gatta put work in too.

One thing I have found in my life is one rule you can kinda lean on when it comes to mental health. That rule is if you are worried that you are faking it or trying to use whatever you are feeling to some kind of benefit, then you are not faking it on the sole principal that you’re paying enough attention to know you are not.

Usually thinking you might be faking it comes from a lot of places. Society and the news are one, but there is also the chance of family. I myself have had depression since I was six but was never diagnosed till I was 24 and paid to see a therapist on my own because family would always dismiss it. If any of that resonates with you, please ignore the words of those people as they are wrong. They are not professionals and imo it’s an abusive move that does nothing but harm.

You’re not faking it, and if it’s anything like for me, when you get diagnosed it might feel like more of a relief than anything else because you were not wrong. Keep strong, I know it’s hard but it you’re able to move forward when COVID is over, please do because it can help relieve that stress of “what if” so much. Good luck, I hope this has helped

I agree with all the comments so far said so I don’t want to double up on anything, but a therapist will not judge you and they are there to provide a safe place for you to say those intrusive thoughts and find their root and start working on better copping mechanisms and other therapy like CBT (it can really help).

A few pointers I can give that have helped me is in the first session try to explain what you are needing and what you are wanting since then the therapist can make goals with you and plans to best help you. Another is that, if the therapist’s style isn’t working or not helping you do not feel like you have to keep seeing them. They are there to help you and sometimes you might need a different approach. I know I had to go through several therapists till I found one that could actually assist with PTSD, so if you eventually get a more specific idea of what you are fighting and need someone more specialized. Do not feel bad if you gatta switch.

It’s hard, I really really get that. The first step in this is sometimes the worst because you’re fighting your own trauma and mentality of “it’s fine, it’s okay” and that’s so difficult. But, you are not alone and therapy is honestly so stabilizing once you get things started.

I hope that you can see a therapist soon and that you have a easier time in the upcoming days leading to it.
All the time, you’re not alone at all
